sentences.text: This small dinosaur measured approximately 2.45 meters in length and weighed about 25 kilograms.
Its unique features included spatulate front teeth, pointed and unserrated maxillary teeth, and a long neck with elongated vertebrae.
The holotype skeleton, catalogued as FPDM-V8461, was discovered in August 2007 within the Kitadani Formation.
Scientists including Yoichi Azuma and Xu Xing formally named and described the species Fukuivenator paradoxus in 2016.
Researchers suggest Fukuivenator adapted to a herbivorous or omnivorous diet due to its long neck and unserrated teeth.
Authors suggested Fukuivenator was not a pure carnivore but adapted to a herbivorous or omnivorous diet due to its long neck and heterodont unserrated teeth.
An initial phylogenetic analysis placed Fukuivenator in an unresolved position within Maniraptoriformes, equally related to ornithomimosaurs, maniraptorans, and Ornitholestes.
However, a 2021 redescription recovered Fukuivenator as the most basal member of the Therizinosauria.
The Kitadani Formation where the fossil was found is estimated to be between 127 and 115 million years old.
According to the Paleobiology Database, the time range for Fukuivenator spans the Aptian, from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
A 2023 analysis supported Migmanychion as the closest relative to Fukuivenator, placing them just outside the Therizinosauria crown group.
